v.why: Raising an already large learning rate causes divergence and a sharp accuracy drop.
Very small learning rates leave the network undertrained in 243 epochs, so increasing them helps substantially.
Stepping back from a divergent learning rate recovers large amounts of accuracy.
Small batches produce noisy gradients, so larger steps destabilize training more.
With a tiny learning rate, fewer updates per epoch from larger batches worsen undertraining.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize training under aggressive learning rates.
Increasing an already strong L2 penalty pushes the model into underfitting.
Relaxing excessive regularization restores capacity and accuracy.
Narrow networks are capacity-limited, so widening helps most there.
Deeper networks are more prone to instability under large learning rates.

raw:
These ten hypotheses come from general knowledge of how MLP training behaves under Adam. I did not compute them from the benchmark tables, so treat them as predictions to test.

1. **Learning rate up, when it is already high:** the gain is lower, because pushing past about 0.08 makes training diverge.
2. **Learning rate up, when it is low:** the gain is higher, because tiny rates leave the model undertrained after 243 epochs.
3. **Learning rate down, when it is high:** the gain is higher, because stepping back from a divergent rate recovers a lot of accuracy.
4. **Learning rate up, when batch size is small:** the gain is lower, because noisy small-batch gradients plus large steps make training unstable.
5. **Batch size up, when learning rate is low:** the gain is lower, because fewer updates per epoch make slow learning even slower.
6. **Batch size up, when learning rate is high:** the gain is higher, because larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize aggressive steps.
7. **L2 penalty up, when it is already high:** the gain is lower, because heavy weight decay causes underfitting.
8. **L2 penalty down, when it is high:** the gain is higher, because relaxing excessive regularization restores capacity.
9. **Width up, when width is small:** the gain is higher, because narrow networks are capacity-limited.
10. **Depth up, when learning rate is high:** the gain is lower, because deeper networks are more fragile under large steps.
